items.prompt: Tasks A (id 1), B (id 2) and C (id 3) are saved. The user deletes C, exits, restarts the app and adds D. Which id does D get?
items.answer: Id 3, as the next id is the highest surviving id plus one
distractors: Id 4, as the next id is stored in tasks.txt with the tasks
Id 1, as a restart starts numbering again from the beginning
Id 4, as deleted ids are written to a list that is never reused
items.explanation: loadTasks calls calculateNextId, which scans the surviving tasks for the highest id and adds one. C is gone from the file, so the highest id is 2 and D gets 3 (reproduced by running the app). No counter is saved; the restart does not reset to 1 because loaded tasks are counted.

items.prompt: In one session, without restarting, the user adds A (id 1) and B (id 2), deletes B, then adds C. Which id does C get?
items.answer: Id 3, since nextId only goes up and deleteTask leaves it alone
distractors: Id 2, since deleteTask recalculates nextId from the tasks left
Id 2, since addTask always reuses the lowest free id first
Id 1, since deleting a task renumbers the remaining tasks
items.explanation: addTask uses nextId and then increments it; deleteTask only removes the task from the list and never touches nextId. Running the app gives "Task added with id 3". Ids are only recalculated in loadTasks, at startup.

items.prompt: tasks.txt holds ten valid tasks plus one stray line reading garbage. The user starts the app and chooses 5 straight away. What is in tasks.txt afterwards?
items.answer: Nothing; the empty fallback list is written over it on exit
distractors: The ten tasks; a failed load switches saving off for that session
The ten tasks; the stray line is skipped and the rest are rewritten
The original bytes; saveTasks does not write when the list is empty
items.explanation: parseTask throws on the line without "=", loadTasksFromDisk falls back to an empty list, and the finally block in run() saves that empty list. newBufferedWriter truncates the file first, so it ends at 0 bytes (reproduced). Nothing disables saving or skips bad lines, and saveTasks writes whatever list it is given.

items.prompt: Task 1 is already completed. The user picks option 3 and enters 1 again. What happens?
items.answer: The app prints "Task not found or already completed." and completedAt keeps its first value
distractors: The app prints "Task marked as completed." and completedAt moves to the current time
The app prints "Task 1 is already completed." and leaves the task exactly as it was
The app flips the task back to incomplete and clears its completedAt timestamp
items.explanation: markCompleted returns false at once when completed is true, so completedAt is not touched. completeTask in App cannot tell "missing" from "already done", so it prints the shared message. There is no undo path and no task-specific message.

items.prompt: At the prompt "Enter the id of the task to delete:" the user types -1. What does the app do?
items.answer: It goes back to the menu without printing any message
distractors: It prints "Please enter a valid whole number." and goes back
It prints "Task not found." because no task has id -1
It deletes the last task, counting back from the end
items.explanation: readTaskId parses -1 successfully and returns it, but -1 is also its error sentinel, so deleteTask sees -1 and returns early with no output (the review checklist notes this). The "valid whole number" message only prints when parseInt throws, and deleteTask in the manager is never called.

items.prompt: Someone hand-edits tasks.txt so one block says completed=yes. What does the app do with that block at startup?
items.answer: It loads the task as not completed, with no error shown
distractors: Loading fails and the app starts with an empty task list
It loads the task as completed, as the value is not empty
It skips that block, and every other task still loads
items.explanation: Boolean.parseBoolean returns true only for "true" (any case) and false for everything else, without throwing. completed is then non-null, so the required-field check passes. The review checklist lists "invalid boolean text silently reading as false" as a subtle bug.

items.prompt: A newer build added a priority=high line inside every task block. This older build loads that file and later saves. What happens to the priority lines?
items.answer: They are ignored on load, and the next save drops them from the file
distractors: Loading fails, as an unknown key counts as an invalid line
They are kept in memory and written back unchanged on save
Their values are appended to each task description on load
items.explanation: The switch in parseTask has an empty default branch, so unknown keys are skipped. saveTasks writes exactly six fixed keys, so the extra data is lost on the next save. An invalid line means one with no "=", which priority=high is not.

items.prompt: A loaded task has completed=true but an empty completedAt. How does option 2 show it?
items.answer: As [X] with a Created line and no Completed line at all
distractors: As [ ], since a task with no completion time counts as open
As [X] with a Completed line copying the created time
It crashes, as formatDate is handed a null date to format
items.explanation: The checkbox depends only on isCompleted(). The Completed line is added only when the task is completed AND completedAt is not null, so it is left out and formatDate is never called with null (reproduced with a hand-written file).

items.prompt: The user adds a task, then the input stream ends (Ctrl+D or a piped script runs out) before option 5 is chosen. What happens to the new task?
items.answer: It is saved, as the finally block runs while the exception escapes
distractors: It is lost, as only choosing option 5 leads to saveTasksToDisk
It is lost, as the exception exits before any save code is reached
It stays unsaved, as the app catches the error and shows the menu again
items.explanation: scanner.nextLine throws NoSuchElementException, which run() does not catch, but the finally block still calls saveTasksToDisk before the exception ends the program. Piping one add with no exit produced a stack trace and a tasks.txt holding the task.

items.prompt: tasks.txt stores the block for id 5 first and the block for id 2 second. In what order does option 2 list them?
items.answer: Id 2 first, as loadTasks sorts the list by id after loading
distractors: Id 5 first, as tasks are kept in the order the file has them
Id 5 first, as the newest createdAt is listed before others
Completed tasks first, and then the open ones sorted by id
items.explanation: TaskManager.loadTasks sorts by Task::getId with Comparator.comparingInt, and listTasks prints getAllTasks in list order. Nothing sorts by createdAt or completion state.

items.prompt: The app starts in a folder that has no tasks.txt at all. What does it print first?
items.answer: "Loaded 0 task(s)." and then the usual menu
distractors: "Could not load tasks. Starting with an empty list."
An error about the missing file, and then it exits
"No tasks found.", as the empty list is printed at startup
items.explanation: loadTasks checks Files.exists and returns an empty list for a missing file, which is a normal case, not an IOException. The fallback message only appears when reading or parsing throws; "No tasks found." belongs to option 2.

items.prompt: A user adds a task titled x=y, exits and restarts. What title does the reloaded task have?
items.answer: x=y, because the line is split at the first = into two parts
distractors: x, because the text after a second = sign is thrown away
y, because the last = sign on the line decides the value
None; the block fails to parse, so loading falls back
items.explanation: parseTask uses line.split("=", 2): the limit 2 stops after the first "=", so the key is "title" and the value is "x=y" (reproduced with a=b). Only a line with no "=" at all is invalid.

items.front: What does TaskManager.getAllTasks return, and why does that matter for callers?
items.back: A new ArrayList copied from the internal list. Callers can loop over or change their copy without adding or removing tasks inside the manager, so every change goes through addTask, completeTask or deleteTask. The Task objects themselves are shared, not copied.

items.front: Why would a newline inside a title or description be dangerous for the tasks.txt format?
items.back: The format is line based: each field is one key=value line and blocks end with a --- line. An embedded newline would split one value across two lines, so the second half would no longer be a key=value line of its own task field. The CLI cannot enter one today because Scanner reads single lines.

items.front: How does the app make sure a new task title is not blank?
items.back: readRequiredLine loops: it prints the prompt, trims the input, and returns it only when it is non-empty; otherwise it prints "This field cannot be empty." and asks again. The description uses a plain nextLine().trim() and may be empty.
